html:
The Manso, who called themselves Tampachoa, were an Indigenous people of the Rio Grande valley around today's El Paso and Las Cruces. They lived by fishing, hunting and gathering along the river, with little farming.

Spanish travellers met them on the road north to New Mexico in the 1580s and 1590s. In 1659 Franciscans founded the mission of Guadalupe for them at El Paso del Norte, now Ciudad Juárez. After the Pueblo Revolt of 1680, Spanish settlers and Pueblo refugees crowded into the area, and the Manso rose against the Spanish in 1684. Over the next century they merged into the mixed population of the El Paso area and with the Apache. Their neighbours included the Janos and Jumano.
